title: Personal Infinitive in Depth
summary: Master when to use personal infinitives with explicit subjects, prepositions, and formal style.

sections.heading: When it is required or strongly preferred
sections.body: Use the personal infinitive when the infinitive has an explicit subject different from the main clause or when the ending prevents ambiguity.

examples.en: It is better for you all to leave now.

examples.pt: O gerente autorizou os funcionários a trabalharem de casa.
examples.en: The manager authorized the employees to work from home.

examples.pt: Para nós chegarmos a tempo, precisamos sair cedo.
examples.en: For us to arrive on time, we need to leave early.

sections.heading: After prepositions and connectors
sections.body: It is especially common after **antes de**, **depois de**, **para**, **por**, **sem**, **ao**, and **apesar de** when the subject is clear or contrastive.

examples.en: After we finish, we'll have dinner.

examples.pt: Apesar de eles morarem longe, vêm sempre.
examples.en: Although they live far away, they always come.

sections.heading: Plain infinitive vs personal infinitive
sections.body: If the subject is generic or identical to the main subject, the plain infinitive is often better. Overusing endings can sound heavy.

examples.pt: É difícil aprender uma língua sozinho.
examples.en: It is hard to learn a language alone.

keyPoints: Personal infinitive clarifies who performs the infinitive action.
It is frequent after prepositions when subjects differ.
Avoid it when the subject is generic or obviously the same.
Formal writing uses it more often than casual speech.

commonMistakes.note: Use personal infinitive after apesar de with explicit subject.
Same subject: plain infinitive is natural.
